correctness.rationale: The state (allocation counts c_j, unique high-good recipient o_i or −1) is a sufficient statistic for every legal online adversarial history. Terminal own and EFX-residual values depend only on this state. Alternating for-all-adversary masks then exists-allocator choices yields an exhaustive five-turn dynamic program. Independently reconstructed finite minimax calculations confirmed a simultaneous H=1,2,4 policy and a separate universal H≥4 predicate; symbolic affine/monotone-quadratic extension proves all real H in the intervals. The explicit adaptive adversary starts with three universal lows, then high masks determined by count pattern and completes missing spikes; all 27×9=243 responses satisfy sharp <=2/H (2≤H≤4) and <=1/2 (H≥4) comparisons. Therefore α*(H)=min{1,max{2/H,1/2}} for exactly five goods/three agents, every-path EFX, and known per-agent one-spike frequencies.
residual_risks: Exhaustion covers precisely five turns, not all horizons.
The continuous H statement depends on inequalities between endpoint checks; enumerating H alone would not prove it.
